Article Title: India win men's compound team gold, archery haul grows to three golds at Asian Games
Article Text:
The Indian team defeated China 238-237 in a thrilling final to clinch the gold medal. (Image credit: X)

NEW DELHI: India continued their strong run in archery at the Asian Games 2026 as the trio of Kushal Dalal, Sahil Jadhav and Ganesh Mani Ratnam won the gold medal in the men's compound team event in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Wednesday.The Indian team defeated China 238-237 in a thrilling final to clinch the gold medal.India held their nerve in a closely fought contest.The men's compound team gold came on a big day for Indian archery.Earlier, the women's compound team of Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep also won gold after beating China 238-234 in the final.India's compound mixed team of Chikitha and Sahil also finished on top after beating South Korea in a shoot-off. The victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the Los Angeles 2028 Games, where the compound mixed team event will make its Olympic debut.The men's team of Dalal, Jadhav and Ganesh had earlier defeated the UAE 235-215 in the round of 16 and Bhutan 235-232 in the quarterfinals.The Indian women's and mixed teams successfully defended the compound team titles won at the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou.
Article Summary: Kushal Dalal, Sahil Jadhav and Ganesh Mani Ratnam win gold in men's compound team event. Indian team defeated China 238-237 in a thrilling final to clinch the gold medal. Earlier, Indian women's team also won gold after beating China in the final.

Article Title: Sports Ministry top brass to skip Asian Games, focus on BRICS Games
Article Text:
File photo of Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao. (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The higher-ranking Sports Ministry officials, including Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, have cancelled their plans to travel to Aichi-Nagoya for the ongoing Asian Games . It has been reliably learnt that the top brass will remain in the country to oversee the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games on October 12-13 in Ahmedabad.Rao, who was scheduled to fly out to Japan on September 28, altered his plans keeping the importance of the BRICS Games in mind. An official from the sports ministry denied reports that the move came because of India's underwhelming show in Japan."Secretary Sports (Rao), being the senior-most officer of the Ministry decided to monitor the preparation of the Games, given the time left for the Games to begin, which would have been difficult to do from Japan. Therefore, he has cancelled his trip to the Asian Games," a source told TimesofIndia.com.It has also been learnt that the Sports Ministry had always intended to keep the officials contingent limited as part of an austerity drive. With the closing ceremony scheduled for October 4, Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) CEO Col. NS Johal is one of the highest-ranking officials available in Aichi-Nagoya.Organisation of the BRICS Games is being coordinated between the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Gujarat government. Around 2,000 athletes, officials and other participants from nine countries, including China, Russia, Iran, Bolivia, are due to attend the non-competitive tournament. The focus of the Games will be on showcasing traditional and indigenous sports and cultural practices from BRICS nations.With India due to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and bidding to host the 2036 Olympics, both in Ahmedabad, successful hosting of the BRICS Games has been considered as critical for the country's image as a sporting nation.
Article Summary: The top brass will remain in the country to oversee the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games. The focus of the Games will be on showcasing traditional and indigenous sports and cultural practices from BRICS nations. Around 2,000 athletes, officials and other participants from nine countries, including China, Russia, Iran, Bolivia, are due to attend the non- competitive tournament.

Article Title: From days without food to CWG gold: Ashmita Dey now faces India's 32-year judo wait at Asian Games
Article Text:
Asmita Dey

When food was a struggle, a house became the dream

Asmit Dey with coach Yashpal Solanki

Father's death, Commonwealth gold and what followed

Asmita Dey with her Father

Asmita Dey has been promoted to DSP in UP Police

A tough Asian Games test

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ashmita Dey arrives at the Asian Games less than two months after becoming the first Indian judoka to win Commonwealth Games gold.The Commonwealth title in Birmingham changed her profile almost overnight, and the 24-year-old, who had spent much of her career out of the spotlight, began to be recognised off the mat too.“No one knew me before. But now everyone knows me. When I went to get food, someone said, this is the same girl, right? This is the same girl who created history for Judo for the first time in India. I was very happy to hear all this,” Ashmita told Timesofindia.comThe recognition means so much to her for a reason. Asmita’s career has been built through a combination of sporting support and financial uncertainty, with the latter shaping much of what she wanted from judo.Before the Commonwealth gold, there had been the bronze at the Asian Junior Championships in 2022, gold at the Junior Asia Cup in Macau in 2023, a silver at the Asian Open in Kuwait later that year, and another podium finish at the African Open in Casablanca in 2025. She had also finished fifth at the Asian Senior Championships in Almaty in April this year.The success and recognition have come a long way from a humble start in Belonia, a small town in Tripura, where her introduction to judo was almost accidental.Her uncle heard about trials at a sports school where there was running, jumping and a fitness test. Asmita had initially been around athletics trials, but judo became the sport that stayed.“My aunt thought I was talented and she put me in Judo and I started from there,” Asmita remembered.Within a week of starting judo, she competed in a jiu-jitsu event and finished first. Two or three weeks later came a state competition, where she won gold.The early years were sustained by family members moving her between places for training. Her brothers ferried her on a cycle for training, while her father would often travel with her from the village on a scooter, sometimes even in the rain.“My father used to support me a lot. He never stopped me for a game. My mother never stopped me.”However, there were limits to what the family could provide. Asmita remembers periods when there was no food at home.“Because sometimes we didn't even have food. We used to sleep after drinking water. Sometimes we only had rice, salt, and chillies with water. Sometimes we used to get food once, sometimes twice. So I remember all those days.”Her mother had one gold earring, the only piece of jewellery she owned, and that was pawned for money. Asmita said she still has not been able to get it back, and the interest has continued to accumulate.Asked if she would get it back now, Asmita’s answer was immediate.“Yes, it will definitely come back. I have to get it.”Her father worked as a bicycle mechanic, taking whatever work he could find as the family struggled to make ends meet. The family lived in rented accommodation for years. Asmita grew up with the idea that a house of their own would have to come from what she could achieve.She had won her first competitions soon after starting, and her coaches were already telling her she could go further.By 2018, she had won silver at the Khelo India Games and moved to the Sports Authority of India Regional Centre in Bhopal. That was when she came under coach Yashpal Solanki - former Indian judoka and an Arjuna Awardee - after earlier support from Manik Lal Deb in Tripura.Solanki also pushed her towards international competition. “My coach used to say that I have to play internationally. I have to win a gold medal. He told me that I have to win a gold medal and have done that”The path, most recently, was interrupted by injury and, more painfully, by the death of her father. When she was injured in Delhi, he had travelled to her with her medicines.“When I was injured for the first time in Delhi, my father came to me. He brought all the medicines for me,” remembered Asmita.His death, in 2025, came with a Commonwealth Games trial coming up, and her coach called her back to training around the 12th or 13th day.There was about a month left.“I told him that I can't do it. I don't want to do it.”The coach then spoke to her about the Bhagavad Gita and death.“He told me that this is the truth. He used to read the Gita. I also read the Gita. He told me that this is the truth. One day, a person has to go. He motivated me a lot.”She returned to training. “To manage myself, I thought that if I cry and get weak, who will take care of my family? How will I make my house? I controlled my emotions a lot. You have to control your emotions a lot.”And before the final, there was only one thought. “I was thinking that I have to win and I have to get the gold medal.”She did, and the gold brought another reminder of the person she had lost. “Yes, I remembered my father a lot. If my father was alive, he would have been very happy. It was such a big achievement for me. He would have been very happy. I know that.”But there was another moment on the Commonwealth podium that stayed with her: the Indian flag and the national anthem, with athletes from other countries standing around her.“That was the biggest thing. I felt very proud.”Ashmita joined the Uttar Pradesh Police in 2023 through the sports quota. She was subsequently promoted to sub-inspector and, after her Commonwealth Games gold, was elevated to deputy superintendent of police (DSP). The job had already given her a measure of financial security and helped her take care of herself and her family.“I was so worried that I did so much in between. I have faced so much financially, but now I don't have to think much about that; I can [train with a] free mind. Now I can do better. I will do better.”The house, though, remains on her mind.“I always wanted to build a house. I had to do something. I had to do something big. Only if I do this, I can build a house. I always used to think like this. Finally, I can build a house now.”Now comes the Asian Games, where Asmita will face a field led by several of Asia's established names in the women's -48kg category.Mongolia's Narantsetseg Ganbaatar is the highest-ranked entrant at No. 13 in the world, followed by Kazakhstan's Abiba Abuzhakynova at No. 19. Japan's Mitsuki Kondo, Uzbekistan's Laziza Haydarova, Hong Kong China's Ka Lee Wong and South Korea's Su Jin Jung are also in the 11-judoka field.There is another number that puts India's task in perspective. Judo has produced only five Asian Games medals for India, all of them bronze. Four came at the sport's debut at the 1986 Seoul Games, while Poonam Chopra won the fifth in the women's 56kg category at Hiroshima in 1994.India has not been on the Asian Games judo podium since. Indian judokas, by comparison, have won 15 Commonwealth Games medals.Asmita is entering a field led by higher-ranked Asian judokas, while carrying an Indian judo record that has not produced an Asian Games medal for 32 years.
Article Summary: Asmita Dey is the first Indian judoka to win Commonwealth Games gold. The 24-year-old has been promoted to DSP in UP Police. Dey's career has been built through a combination of sporting support and financial uncertainty, with the latter shaping much of what she wanted from judo.

Article Title: Vithya ran, Nithya prayed: The twin bond behind India’s new 400m hurdles record
Article Text:
Vithya Ramraj with her twin Nithya

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chennai: Far away from Aichi-Nagoya, at a gym in Chennai, Nithya Ramraj was too scared to watch Monday’s women’s 400m hurdles at the Asian Games live. She had her eyes tightly shut, either in prayer, pure fear or both.It was only when Nithya’s friends at the gym informed her that Vithya Ramraj had shattered the national record and won bronze that her twin sister opened her eyes.Vithya dedicated breaking PT Usha ’s 42-year-old record to the person who had been rooting for her all along. For the Ramraj twins, moments like these are never individual ones to celebrate. Over the years, they have been each other’s strength, offering support and a helping hand whenever needed.Nithya, a 100m hurdler, was in the Chennai gym and not in Aichi-Nagoya because she is recovering from an ankle injury.“We knew she would break the national record, but we were waiting to see when it would happen. Vithya always calls me before and after she finishes a race. I just tell her to focus on the race and that we will be rewarded for the hard work. After I came to know that I would miss the Asian Games, she told me not to worry and said, ‘I will do double of what you would have done had you been part of the Asian Games.’That is why she dedicated the medal to me,” Nithya told TOI on Tuesday.Their support for each other has found tangible measure. In 2021, after Nithya secured a job at Income Tax, she supported Vithya financially. Last year, the roles were reversed as Vithya stepped in to take care of Nithya and the family’s needs.Once Vithya equalled Usha’s record in 2023, there were always questions about when she would break it.“I have seen her struggles closely over the past three years, and that is why I was confident she would break the national record. I tell her that God has given her wings, and I ask her to lend them to me so that I can also run as fast as her. Unlike me, she is a very dedicated athlete,” said Nithya.While Vithya and Nithya chase their dreams on the track, their mother quietly misses having her daughters around.“It has been almost a year since Vithya last came home. Once we get married, we cannot spend as much time with our parents, and with the tight training schedule, we hardly get to go home now,” said Nithya.
Article Summary: Vithya dedicated breaking PT Usha’s 42-year-old record to the person who had been rooting for her all along. Nithya was in the Chennai gym and not in Aichi- Nagoya because she is recovering from an ankle injury.

Article Title: One win from Olympic ticket: India face South Korea in Asian Games hockey semifinal
Article Text:
India's women's hockey team at Asian Games

Gold carries a prize that goes beyond the medal: a direct ticket to the Olympics. That makes Wednesday’s semifinal against South Korea a significant hurdle for India.A place in the final would put Salima Tete and Co within one win of the Asian Games title and the direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.India have been rampant so far, producing their best league-phase campaign at the Asian Games. They won all five matches, scoring an astonishing 66 goals, the best figure among the 12 teams in the competition, while conceding just three.Deepika has led the charge with 21 goals, while Navneet Kaur has contributed 10 and Rutuja Pisal seven.Chief coach Sjoerd Marijne was pleased with the balance in India’s attack, with 34 field goals coming alongside 30 from penalty corners.“It’s good that different players have scored and this always gives a boost to the confidence of players and this will definitely help,” he told TOI on the eve of the semifinal.But South Korea represents a different challenge. The league phase offered India little resistance; the semifinal will. South Korea finished second behind defending champions China in Group B.
Article Summary: India face South Korea in the Asian Games women's hockey semifinal. India have won all five matches in the league phase. They have scored 66 goals, the best figure among the 12 teams in the competition. South Korea finished second behind defending champions China in Group B.

Article Title: Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna power India into squash semifinals, medal assured at Asian Games
Article Text:
India's Anahat Singh, right, shakes hands with Tanvi Khanna (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s women’s squash team assured itself of an Asian Games medal after defeating Singapore 2-0 to progress to the semifinals on Wednesday. Tanvi Khanna set the tone with a gritty victory in the opening singles, overcoming Au Yeong Wai Iynn 11-6, 4-11, 15-13, 11-1 in a 32-minute contest.After being pushed in the second game, Tanvi regained control to edge a closely fought third game 15-13 before closing out the match comfortably in the fourth.In the second singles, young Anahat Singh, a silver medallist in the individual event, produced a dominant performance to beat Au Yeong Wai Yhann 11-7, 11-3, 11-4 in just 22 minutes.With India taking an unassailable 2-0 lead, veteran Joshna Chinappa did not need to take the court. Joshna had earlier won a bronze medal in the mixed doubles event.India will face its semifinal opponent at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena on Thursday, with the team now assured of adding another medal to its Asian Games tally.The Indian women had finished their Pool C campaign with a 3-0 win over Iran on Tuesday. They had earlier defeated China and Japan in their opening two group matches.The medal assurance comes on a day when India also secured another major archery triumph.Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep defeated China 238-234 in the women’s compound team final to retain the Asian Games gold medal.The Indian compound team equalled Korea’s world record score with the victory. China’s Wunier, Yue Wang and Fangyao Wei took silver, while South Korea’s Park Jungyoon, Park Yerin and Kang Yeonseo defeated Chinese Taipei to win bronze.India had also beaten South Korea 234-233 in the semifinal to reach the final. The women’s compound team had won gold at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou as well.
Article Summary: India's women's squash team assured itself of an Asian Games medal after defeating Singapore 2-0. Tanvi Khanna set the tone with a gritty victory in the opening singles. India will face its semifinal opponent at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena on Thursday.

Article Title: Parveen Hooda’s redemption fight: From 22-month ban and lost medal to Asian Games final
Article Text:
Ankush Panghal and Parveen Hooda (IANS/PTI Photos)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As Parveen Hooda unleashes fury inside the ring, she is fighting battles far beyond it. The Rohtak boxer is punching at more than an opponent now. Every counter carries the weight of a medal taken away, an Olympic dream that vanished and a family waiting for relief.The road here has been paved with setbacks, sacrifice and a hunger for redemption.Three years ago, Parveen won bronze at the Hangzhou Games. Then came the whereabouts failure, a 22-month suspension and the stripping of her medal. The Paris Olympics slipped away. Her Glasgow CWG return in July-August ended in a quarterfinal defeat.Now, in Aichi-Nagoya, she has fought her way back to the final, beating China’s Li Shu 5-0 in the 65kg semifinal.A silver is assured. But Parveen is not looking back. She wants gold and full redemption.Her fight has always extended beyond the ring. Her father, Lakhpat Hooda, has been battling cancer for four years and is also a heart patient. Her mother, Neelam Devi, sells buffalo milk to keep the household running, while Parveen’s 20-year-old younger brother is studying.An ITBP Assistant Sub-Inspector, Parveen has become the family’s principal breadwinner.“Parveen takes care of every need of the family,” her childhood coach Sudhir Hooda told TOI. “She has been funding her father’s medical treatment with cash awards from boxing and her ITBP income.”Hooda first saw Parveen in April 2010. She was in Class 5, barely 22kg, and came from a family that struggled to afford boxing nutrition.“I became the village sarpanch and opened an academy in Rohtak to keep youngsters away from drugs and crime, offering 80 children free coaching, milk and diet. Parveen was one of the brightest.”Ankush Panghal provided another headline, stunning Uzbekistan’s Fazliddin Erkinboev 4-1 in the 80kg semifinal.After dropping the opening round, Ankush changed gears, attacked the body and dominated the finish. He is India’s first male Asian Games finalist since Amit Panghal in 2018.Narender Berwal secured bronze after a 0-5 loss to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan in the +90kg semifinal. It is his second straight Asian Games bronze.
Article Summary: Parveen Hooda beats China's Li Shu 5-0 in the 65kg semifinal. Her father, Lakhpat Hooda, has been battling cancer for four years and is also a heart patient. Her mother, Neelam Devi, sells buffalo milk to keep the household running.

Article Title: India’s new-ball puzzle: West Indies series offers young pacers a chance to stake claim
Article Text:
India's Prasidh Krishna, right, with Nitish Kumar Reddy (PTI Photo)

Kohli’s happy-hunting ground

Greaves out of 2nd ODI

Guwahati: With the ODI World Cup in South Africa just a year away, the Indian team management’s priority now is to identify the bowling combinations. A big part of the process is trying out different new-ball bowlers in the ongoing ODI series against West Indies.“You may see different bowlers taking the new ball because it is important for us to assess how these young players respond under pressure,” spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule said on the eve of the second ODI.It may be noted that India don’t have the services of Jasprit Bumrah for this series as he is part of the T20I team currently in the Asian Games in Japan.In the first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, India opened the bowling with seam-bowling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy and Prasidh Krishna after benching Mohammed Siraj. Reddy’s only over with the new ball, however, yielded 18 runs.The team management must continue working on creating backup resources for the injury-prone Bumrah and Hardik Pandya.Bahutule stressed that identifying the right pace attack for South African conditions remains a key objective over the next 12 months.“We are aware of the type of pitches we’re likely to encounter in South Africa. The focus is on identifying players who can have the most impact in those conditions,” he added.The experiments are likely to continue.“These series are a good opportunity for us to see different combinations. We want to understand which bowlers can operate effectively in different phases of the innings,” Bahutule said.One bowler who has already strengthened his case is Kuldeep Yadav. The left-arm wrist-spinner produced another match-winning display in the opening ODI, ensuring India stayed in control.Bahutule described Kuldeep as “a match-winner for India” and praised both his work ethic and ability to deliver in any conditions. Kuldeep is expected to compete for the lead spinner’s spot in the XI when India reach South Africa for the World Cup.There are fewer concerns on the batting front. One may expect another run feast on Wednesday.Kohli has played two ODIs at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium, scored two centuries and walked away as the Player of the Match on both occasions.Justin Greaves, who scored a century in the first ODI, has been ruled out with a calf injury.
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav is expected to compete for the lead spinner’s spot in the XI when India reach South Africa for the World Cup. Justin Greaves, who scored a century in the first ODI, has been ruled out with a calf injury. Jasprit Bumrah is part of the T20I team currently in the Asian Games in Japan.

Article Title: No TV, no smartphone, just a phone call: How Neeru Dhanda’s gold reached her mother
Article Text:
Neeru Dhanda

A journey that began by a pond

A mother’s unwavering faith

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya/Jind: Clutching her BPL card, Sudesh Devi was walking from her one-room house towards the village PDS ration shop in Haryana’s Sangatpura on Tuesday morning when her battered keypad phone buzzed. It was an unknown number.“Neeru gold jeeti hai, Asiad mein (Neeru has won gold, at Asiad),” said the stranger.She stopped in her tracks. Fighting back the urge to jump for joy, she looked around for someone to verify the news.“We don’t have a TV or smartphone. I hadn’t been able to follow the news but knew last night that Neeru was to compete,” she told TOI later.Devi, 48, collected the ration and hurried back home in a daze.“I still couldn’t believe she won gold,” she said.In Nagoya, meanwhile, at a rain-swept, high-altitude shooting range, Neeru Dhanda was making a mother’s dream come true, becoming the first Indian woman, and the first Indian since the late Randhir Singh in 1978, to win gold in individual trap.India had won seven shooting gold medals at the last edition in Hangzhou but has endured a difficult campaign here. Neeru provided the country’s first gold in shooting at these Games, less than two weeks after she lay on a hospital bed, not even sure she would make the trip.Neeru had spent three days in a Bhopal hospital with suspected H1N1 flu while the national camp was under way in the city. On a liquid diet for five days, she could not get to the practice station for three-and-a-half weeks and arrived in Nagoya short of training, but not intent.On the eve of her gold-winning effort, you would not know she had been through all that.On Tuesday, rain landed on her hand and threatened to cause a disturbance. But Neeru stayed locked on to the target.“Aaj agar toofan bhi aa jaye, neeche nahi dekhna (Even if there is a storm, look it in the eye),” she told herself.The storm never came close to derailing her.But it was such a different story just a fortnight ago, when she was riddled with doubt and frail with illness. It was her personal coach Mansher Singh, a three-time silver winner in team trap, who kept her going. On the eve of her event, national coach Peter Wilson gave her a simple message: “Grind it out.”Grinding it out is something Neeru has done since she picked up a shotgun less than a decade ago.Her journey started on the banks of a talaab (pond) close to their home.“My uncle took me to a pond and asked me to shoot a small sheet of tin. I also told myself, ‘Let’s see what I can do.’ I passed that test,” Neeru told TOI.Neeru was then inspired by her cousin Lakshay Sheoran, a silver winner in trap at the 2018 Asian Games.By 2019, she had packed her bags and moved to Bhopal because the Madhya Pradesh Shooting Academy offered free guns to its trainees. But before she could get her hands on one, she had to prove she could shoot.Uncle Somveer, Lakshay’s father and a former national wrestling champion, handed her an old country double-barrel gun and took her to the pond. It was almost as if the family was indulging a petulant kid. Today, they would be so happy that they gave in to her demands.“We had neither the money nor the resources for this sport. Lakshay helped arrange everything. My daughter even practised with his rifle. His family is related to us. Today, after seeing what my daughter has achieved, my heart is filled with happiness,” father Suresh said.Behind her achievement lies a story of extraordinary struggle, sacrifice and a mother’s unwavering faith in her daughter. Poverty was just another battle on the way.Sudesh Devi took to selling buffalo milk to keep the shared dream alive.When TOI reached their one-room home, the proud mother was washing utensils. Eyes wide in wonder, she looked up and said, “You are telling me it is indeed gold? My Neeru has won gold?”And then she threw up her soap-streaked arms and let out a cheer.Soon, the stream of badhaais started. Villagers flocked in to celebrate ‘Jind ki beti’. Neeru’s feat is all the more remarkable considering that Sangatpura lies in the heart of ‘khap-land’.Father Suresh Dhanda, 56, said the family struggled to support her sporting career but never gave up.Sudesh Devi said she never regretted having daughters.“If God had given me another daughter, I would have welcomed her too. Today, daughters are proving that they can be at the forefront of everything. In the toughest of times, Neeru would tell me, ‘Ma, keep faith in me and ignore what the world says’,” she said.Neeru had decided to put marriage on hold because she wanted to first change her family’s circumstances.“She had promised me that she would first build a good house for the family and start her own family only after fulfilling that promise. After today’s victory, it feels as if all our dreams have come true,” she said.
Article Summary: Neeru Dhanda became the first Indian woman to win gold in individual trap at the Asian Games. She had spent three days in a Bhopal hospital with suspected H1N1 flu. She arrived in Nagoya short of training, but not intent. Her personal coach Mansher Singh kept her going.

Article Title: Supreme Court puts RCA election results on hold after 35 vote, three districts abstain
Article Text:
RCA elections conclude amid SC stay over result

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jaipur: Voting for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections concluded here on Tuesday under the shadow of a Supreme Court directive halting the announcement of results. The apex court's stay came following petitions challenging the complete exclusion of women from the electoral rolls and a legal dispute over the inclusion of three newly formed districts in the voter list. Out of a total of 38 eligible voters, 35 cast their votes while three new districts, Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara and Balotra, voluntarily refrained from polling. Following the court order, the ballot boxes were sealed and deposited in the collectorate treasury without counting, extending the state body’s long history of delayed election outcomes.The polling day was also marked by sharp exchanges between the two presidential post candidates, with Dhananjay Singh Khimsar raising questions over ‘unauthorized presence’ inside the venue and Brij Kishore Upadhyay dismissing the charges while expressing full confidence in his victory.Meanwhile, election officer AK Pandey confirmed that polling was conducted smoothly.“Voting commenced and concluded peacefully. Three new districts did not vote.They submitted in writing that they chose not to vote out of their own free will. In the meantime, we received information that the Supreme Court has issued an order directing that the results of this election should not be declared. Consequently, we have sealed the ballot box and stored it safely until further orders,” Pandey said.Khimsar questioned the presence of outsiders inside the premises and raised concerns over the decision of three districts to skip voting despite attending the AGM before the polling began.“We completely respect the decision of the Supreme Court, but we have registered a formal written complaint regarding irregularities. Why were 11 or 12 individuals who had no connection with cricket allowed entry inside the venue, despite strict identity checks at the gate, if not to influence voters? Representatives from Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara and Balotra attended the AGM, but did not vote, which raises serious concerns,” Khimsar added while maintaining that there is no internal factionalism with the BJP.Upadhyay rejected the allegations of voter influence and announced plans to move the court for an early declaration of results.“RCA voting was conducted in a very peaceful manner and we fully respect the court’s decision. Regarding the allegations of unauthorized people, these are baseless claims typical during election time. The location has a common cafeteria where media and friends sit, but the polling area was completely separate. Association secretaries are experienced individuals who cannot be influenced by people sitting in a cafeteria,” Upadhyay said. “The three district associations refrained from voting voluntarily out of respect for the judiciary after learning about the court order. We plan to file an application to become a party in court to request an early declaration, and we are 100% confident of victory once the results are opened,” he added.The election officer said that there is no scope to act upon complaints. “While polling was ongoing, no complaints were received. After polling concluded, when we were busy with the sealing process, we received two or three complaints. However, at this stage, there is no scope to act upon them. Everything has now been sealed in the ballot box, and the results will be declared once permission is received from the Supreme Court,” Pandey added.Om Prakash Beniwal, representing Didwana-Kuchaman said that their decision was taken to avoid prolonging the legal dispute.“The three of us decided voluntarily that we will not participate in this voting, so that the results don’t get affected or delayed by the court for a long time,” Beniwal said.
Article Summary: Voting for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections concluded under the shadow of a Supreme Court directive halting the announcement of results. Out of a total of 38 eligible voters, 35 cast their votes while three new districts, Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara and Balotra, voluntarily refrained from polling. The ballot boxes were sealed and deposited in the collectorate treasury without counting.

Former India bowler Mohit Sharma is set to join the Zaheer Khan-led Chennai Super Kings (CSK) support staff as the bowling coach starting next season.The development was confirmed by CSK CEO Kasi Viswanathan. "Mohit will join CSK as our new bowling coach. His name was recommended by our head coach Zaheer Khan. Mohit was tremendous with us as a player as well and we hope he will do a great job as bowling coach," Viswanathan told TimesofIndia.com."The next set of coaching staffs will also be recruited on Zaheer's recommendation in the coming weeks," he added.Mohit last played in the Indian Premier League ( IPL ) for the Delhi Capitals but has had two stints with CSK previously, spanning four seasons. He replaces Eric Simmons as the bowling coach.The 38-year-old Mohit has played 120 fixtures in the IPL and has 134 wickets to his name. He had a second wind of sorts during his time at Gujarat Titans, where he emerged as the side's consistent wicket-taker due to his variety and accuracy. Sharma picked up 41 wickets in the two seasons he spent at GT. He also represented Punjab Kings from 2016 to 2018.The Haryana bowler announced his retirement from professional cricket in December last year."Today, with a full heart, I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket. From representing Haryana to wearing the India jersey and playing in the IPL, this journey has been nothing short of a blessing.""A very special thank you to the Haryana Cricket Association for being the backbone of my career. And my deepest gratitude to Anirudh Sir, whose constant guidance and belief in me shaped my path in ways words cannot express.Thank you to the BCCI, my coaches, my teammates, IPL franchises, support staff and all my friends for their love and support," Mohit wrote in an emotional retirement post.His journey with the Indian team will be remembered for the 2015 World Cup under MS Dhoni, where he was the joint third-highest wicket-taker. As far as the IPL is concerned, 2014 was his best outing — he won the Purple Cap after taking 23 wickets — and it came in CSK's colours.Mohit has played 26 ODIs and eight T20Is for India and picked up 31 and six wickets, respectively.

NEW DELHI: Rohit Sharma has opened up on his long-standing bond with Virat Kohli , describing a relationship built on camaraderie, mutual respect and a shared commitment to the Indian cause, while insisting that little has changed between the two despite their evolving roles.Rohit Sharma, speaking to JioStar ahead of India's second ODI against West Indies on Wednesday, shared his thoughts on his relationship with Kohli and revealed how the two continue to exchange ideas about their batting and the team's goals.The pair have been teammates for almost two decades, with Rohit making his India debut in 2007 and Kohli following a year later. From sharing the dressing room to leading India at different stages, their careers have been closely intertwined.“I think we were together. This started, I think, when we were playing in Australia, or right after Australia when we came to India. That's when this started, and whenever this plays on TV, we look at each other and laugh. Which is good, it's fun. People want masala, so there you go, there is some masala,” Rohit said.Rohit said the different personalities and methods of the two batters have never affected their shared objective.“Both of us, we've almost started playing at the same time. I made my debut in 2007, he made his debut in 2008. And since then, we've been trying to give our best for the team. So yeah, there's a strong camaraderie between the two of us,” he said.“We understand what it requires to be at a certain level when you're playing at this level. Methods are different, obviously, but that's how it should be, every individual is different.”Rohit was also emphatic about Kohli's contribution to Indian cricket and what he expects from his former captain going forward.“For what he has done for the team, for this team, there is no question, there is no asking what has he done. It's there for everyone to see it,” Rohit said.“And what he is going to do from here on now, I don't think anything has changed. He'll be the same Kohli that we know of: wants to come, prepare well, go get the runs, win games for Team India.”Rohit added that the same team-first approach remained evident irrespective of who was leading India.“When he was captain, pretty much the same. When I was captain, pretty much the same. And I don't see any reason why anything needs to change,” he said.Rohit also revealed that the two continue to have conversations about their individual games, with their mutual appreciation extending beyond their performances on the field.“Appreciation, appreciation if something good has happened, it has always been there from both sides. I appreciate what he has done, you know, when he took over as a captain with the Test team, especially. It was brilliant, what he did with that team,” Rohit said.“At the same time, there has been a lot of discussion about how both of us as individuals can improve our own game. So, sometimes if something is happening with my batting, he comes and mentions it, sometimes I mention it.”On the upcoming World Cup, Rohit said there was no need for him to explain its importance to Kohli, who has already played four 50-over World Cups.“No, no. He has been playing for so many years. Whether it's the '27 World Cup or the '23 World Cup, there's no need to explain it to him. World Cup is World Cup,” Rohit said.The two may now spend less time together away from cricket, but Rohit said their connection remains unchanged.“Now both of us are spending more time at home, which is always nice,” he said.(Watch Rohit Sharma’s exclusive interview on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network, September 30)(Watch the ICC Men’s ODI World Cup schedule announcement on JioHotstar and Star Sports, October 1)
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have been teammates for almost two decades. Rohit made his India debut in 2007 and Kohli following a year later. The two continue to exchange ideas about their batting and the team's goals. Kohli will be the same Kohli that we know of, says Rohit.

Abishek Porel has been included in Bengal’s senior men’s squad for practice matches against Assam at the ACA Stadium in Guwahati, marking his return to the state side after his arrest in a case involving allegations of rape and other sexual offences.The Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) announced the squad on Tuesday, with Sudip Chatterjee named captain. He was subsequently produced before the Chinsurah court, where the judge directed the police to examine electronic devices in his possession.Police later arrested another friend of Porel as well as the woman complainant in connection with the case.Porel’s selection in the Bengal squad comes just over a week after he was granted bail and puts him back in the state setup ahead of the new domestic season.Sudip Chatterjee (Captain), Abhimanyu Easwaran, Ankur Paul, Ankit Shukla, Sumanta Gupta, Subham Chatterjee, Abishek Porel (W.K.), Shakir Habib Gandhi (W.K.), Pradipta Pramanik, Karan Lal, Aamir Gani, Soummyadip Mandal, Suraj Sindhu Jaiswal, Md. Thiruvananthapuram: West Indies were comfortably placed at 107 for no loss when Kuldeep Yadav was brought into the attack in the 16th over. Fourteen balls into his spell, West Indies opener John Campbell top-edged a tossed-up delivery to short fine leg, giving India the breakthrough they needed.Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill would later soak in the applause for their batting. But it was Kuldeep who helped India turn the game around at the Greenfield International Stadium with flight, dip and guile.Kuldeep is a rhythm bowler. In his nine-year international career, whenever he hits his stride early, he reaps dividends. Sunday was a case in point. Kuldeep showcased his full repertoire, from the tossed-up delivery above the batter’s eyeline and the wrong one to the quickish fuller delivery. He displayed all his wares to finish with 4/40 and win the Player of the Match award.“Personally, I liked my rhythm. Just varying the pace and trying to read the batters, where they are going to hit me,” Kuldeep said after India’s eight-wicket win.“Sometimes to get that confidence back you need to have a spell like this,” the 31-year-old added.For a man with Kuldeep’s skill set, it is baffling why he gets so little match time.Since his debut in 2017, Kuldeep has taken 198 wickets in this format at an average of nearly 27. Of the 10 ODIs and 28 T20Is India have played this year, he has featured in five and four games respectively.Even Kuldeep’s long-form career has been a start-stop affair, featuring sporadically in 19 Tests since his debut against Australia in Dharamshala in 2017.“Kuldeep needs to be handled with care and used as a wicket-taking bowler. The more he bowls, the better he gets because it will help him get into rhythm. We were surprised that Kuldeep has been benched for so many games. Kuldeep is a match-winner and is one of the few mystery bowlers in the world,” former India left-arm spinner Venkatapathy Raju told TOI.Raju believes Kuldeep is a master of deception, capable of taking the pitch out of the equation.“Sometimes for the sake of team combinations you may have to drop Kuldeep. But you need to use him for all the crucial games. Kuldeep is India’s trump card in the 2027 World Cup because of the variety and wicket-taking ability,” Raju added.

NEW DELHI: Neeru Dhanda added another medal to her impressive Asian Games campaign as she teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the gold medal in the trap mixed event at the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Wednesday.The Indian pair finished on 34 points to clinch the gold medal.Qatar won the silver with 32 points, while the People's Republic of China took the bronze with 23 points.For Neeru, it was her third medal at the Asian Games 2026.She had earlier won a silver medal in the women's trap team event before creating history by becoming the first Indian female shooter to win an individual gold medal in trap shooting.Neeru's third medal came alongside Chenai, with the Indian pair producing a strong performance across the four series. India scored 6 points in the first series, 16 in the second, 26 after the third and finished on 34 points.With the gold in the mixed event, Neeru now has a gold and silver in the individual and team events, respectively, besides the mixed team gold.
Article Summary: Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai win gold medal in trap mixed event. Indian pair finish on 34 points to clinch the gold medal. Qatar won the silver with 32 points, while the People's Republic of China took the bronze with 23 points.

Article Title: Shoot-off thriller! Chikitha-Sahil win India’s second archery gold at Asian Games 2026, seal LA28 quota
Article Text:
India’s Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav celebrate after winning gold in the compound mixed team event at the 2026 Asian Games. The duo edged South Korea 20-19 in a shoot-off after the final was tied at 157-157.

India’s compound archery campaign at the Asian Games produced another gold medal on Wednesday as Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav held their nerve to edge South Korea in a dramatic shoot-off.The Indian pair finished the regulation contest locked at 157-157 against South Korea’s Yonghee Choi and Park Jungyoon. With the gold medal decided by a shoot-off, India produced 20 points, while Korea managed 19 to clinch the title.The victory gave India its second gold medal in archery at the Asian Games on Wednesday. Earlier in the day, the Indian women’s compound team comprising Jyothi Surekha Vennam and Prithika Pradeep had beaten China to claim goldThe triumph also carries significance beyond the Asian Games. The result secures India a a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where compound archery is set to make its Olympic debut.

Article Title: Gold again! India beat China and match world record in Asian Games final

India retained the women’s compound archery gold medal at the Asian Games on Wednesday, producing a dominant performance against China and matching the world record score in the process.The Indian trio of Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep defeated China 238-234 in the gold medal match at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park to claim the top spot on the podium.India equalled Korea’s world record score with the victory.China, represented by Wunier, Yue Wang and Fangyao Wei, had to settle for silver.The Indian team had earlier edged South Korea 234-233 in the semifinal to book its place in the title clash. Article Title: India's League of Legends team returns to Asian Games with Hangzhou lessons
Article Text:
S8UL's League of Legends team that is set to represent India at Asian Games 2026

A game that demands five players to think as one

The group that stayed together

Six players, six different routes

What Hangzhou left behind

The gap India is still trying to close

South Korea, Chinese Taipei and Hong Kong await

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At 24, Akshaj Shenoy is heading back to the Asian Games as captain of India's League of Legends team. But becoming a professional player was never part of the original plan.He started playing for fun. Then came the tournaments, better opponents and more time spent understanding the competitive side of the game. There was no single moment when he decided esports would become a profession.“It happened gradually as I got better opportunities and started seeing how far I could take it,” Shenoy told Timesofindia.com.By the time India reached the Asian Games in Hangzhou, Shenoy was studying Economics, Sociology and Industrial Relations while playing professionally and coordinating practice with teammates based in different cities.Three years on, he is returning as the captain and four of the six players who will represent India in League of Legends at Aichi-Nagoya were part of the Hangzhou campaign, where India finished fifth. Ahmed Shahid and Rahul Bisht are the two newcomers.“We look back at Hangzhou with a lot of pride, but also knowing that we could have gone further,” Shenoy said. “Once you've experienced that stage and seen that you can compete with some of the best teams in Asia, you naturally feel that there's more you can achieve.”League of Legends is a 5v5 team-based strategy game in which players control unique characters, known as champions, and work together to destroy the opposing team’s Nexus, the central structure in their base. Each team has five roles, namely Top, Jungle, Mid, ADC and Support, with each serving a different function. Players have different roles and responsibilities, but at the professional level, communication and decision-making are as important as individual skill.“You're constantly thinking about where the opponents could be, what they might do next and how you should respond,” Shenoy said. “At the same time, you're managing your own resources, positioning, timing and trying to make decisions based on what your teammates are doing.”The game was launched in 2009 and has grown into one of the world's major esports titles, with professional competitions across regions and an annual World Championship.For India, however, the challenge is less about finding people who play the game and more about creating enough high-level competition for players to develop against. Shenoy has seen that difference first-hand.After Hangzhou, some of the Indian players continued competing together in domestic and South Asian League of Legends tournaments. They played more tournaments, won titles and spent more time as a unit. That continuity also gave them a better understanding of how each player communicates and reacts in different situations.S8UL signed the group in 2025, giving the players a more structured environment around training and competition.For S8UL co-founder and CEO Animesh Agarwal, that continuity is one of the roster's biggest strengths. He said the players had spent years “playing together, adapting to different competitive environments and developing a strong understanding of each other's game”.The roster won Legends Ascend South Asia in 2025 and later competed in the LCP Promotion Wild Card Playoffs, finishing fifth.“Playing against stronger regional teams gave us valuable experience and showed us where we still needed to improve,” Shenoy said.Shenoy is the most obvious link between the two Asian Games campaigns.The Kochi-based 24-year-old was part of India's Hangzhou team and his esports career has run alongside education and work. Before Hangzhou, he was studying three subjects while playing professionally and coordinating practice sessions for teammates based in different cities. His parents, he said, were supportive of his choices.Today, he is preparing for an MBA and helps with his father's business.Back home, much of his day goes into studying and working on the business. Around 8 pm, he gets online with his teammates, with practice often continuing until 1 am because everyone has different studies and jobs to work around.“I've always enjoyed gaming and, more importantly, the competitive side of esports, so it remains a big part of my life,” he said.Mihir Ranjan is an IIM Ahmedabad graduate based in Delhi. Aakash Shandilya is from Noida and works as a cloud engineering intern. Sanindhya Malik is based in Mauritius and works with Telecommunications Consultants India Ltd.Ahmed Shahid, a Chemical Engineering graduate from Aligarh, and 29-year-old Rahul Bisht, a product designer and entrepreneur from Bengaluru, are making their Asian Games debuts.The six players arrive at Aichi-Nagoya with very different lives outside the game. For most of them, esports has had to fit around education, jobs and other responsibilities rather than replace them.The first Asian Games appearance gave Shenoy a different understanding of what it meant to play for India. “What I remember most is walking out there and realising that we were representing India on such a huge stage,” Shenoy said. “There was a lot of pride, but also a sense of responsibility that came with wearing the India jersey.”The experience also showed the players what was required to compete against Asia's strongest teams. “We've had a few years since then to grow together, compete at a higher level and understand what it takes to perform on a stage like this,” he said.The four returning players know what the stage feels like. Ahmed has been around the group for a long time despite making his Asian Games debut, while Rahul has adapted quickly during the preparations, according to Shenoy.“At the end of the day, we trust each other, and my job is to make sure everyone feels comfortable enough to play their own game when the pressure is at its highest.”Shenoy has also seen India's esports environment become more organised since Hangzhou, with more tournaments, organisations and opportunities for players. But he believes the gap with the leading League of Legends regions remains clear.“The biggest difference is probably the amount of regular high-level competition and the depth of the player pool,” Shenoy said.In Korea, China and Vietnam, players are surrounded by strong competition and have more opportunities to test themselves against high-level opposition.Indian players have had to be more proactive in finding those opportunities. “In India, we've had to be more proactive about finding those opportunities and learning from every international event we get to play,” Shenoy said.Playing together consistently has helped the group develop its communication and understanding, while S8UL has provided a more professional environment around the team.Joining the organisation, Shenoy said, gave the players more support with training and preparation and the confidence to look beyond India. “It also gave us more confidence to look beyond the Indian ecosystem and take international competition seriously,” he said.But he sees a longer-term requirement for the game in India.“There are more organisations, tournaments and opportunities for players to build a career,” Shenoy said. “At the same time, League of Legends still needs a deeper player pool and more regular high-level competition in India.”For the next generation, he wants clearer pathways into competitive play. “The interest and talent are definitely there. The next step is building an ecosystem that can sustain that talent over the long term.”India has been drawn alongside South Korea (2022 Asian Games Gold Medallist), Chinese Taipei (2022 Asian Games Silver Medallist) and Hong Kong in Group B at Aichi-Nagoya. For Shenoy, the group offers a direct measure of how much Indian League of Legends has developed.The established Asian regions have deeper player pools and more regular high-level competition. Playing against them means testing how quickly the Indian players can make decisions, adapt and respond under pressure, but India is not travelling simply to observe.“We don't want to go in thinking we're simply there to learn,” Shenoy said. “We've prepared seriously and we want to compete.”“What they see on stage is the result of years of work behind the scenes,” he said. “There are countless hours of practice, travelling, studying the game and balancing esports with education, jobs and life outside gaming.”“For us, wearing the India jersey is something we've worked towards for a long time. It's a huge responsibility, but it's also a privilege.”
Article Summary: Akshaj Shenoy, 24, is the captain of India's League of Legends team. The Kochi- based 24-year-old was part of the India's Hangzhou team. Four of the six players who will represent India at Aichi-Nagoya were part of Hangzhou.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026 Day 10: Neeru Dhanda, women’s 4x400m relay shine as 8-medal haul takes India past 50
Article Text:
Gold medalist team India pose on the podium following the women's 4x400-meter relay final. (AP Photo)

Neeru braves rain to make history

India's Manisha Keer, Ashima Ahlawat and Neeru Dhanda pose with the national flag. (PTI Photo)

Women’s relay delivers second gold

Gulveer completes medal treble

Bronze medalist Gulveer Singh of India. (AP Photo)

Boxing continues to deliver

Volleyball team stages stunning comeback

Archers make progress

Squash, tennis add wins

NEW DELHI: Neeru Dhanda delivered India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the women’s trap event despite heavy rain and chilly conditions, before the women’s 4x400m relay team added another gold in the evening to make Tuesday a fruitful Day 10 for India at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.The golden double helped India breach the 50-medal mark and climb back into the top 10 of the overall medal standings. India ended the day with 53 medals — six gold, 21 silver and 26 bronze — to sit 10th in the table.The two gold medals also ended India’s wait for a top podium finish after two days without a gold, following the double triumph in kabaddi on September 26.Dhanda produced one of the standout performances of the Games as she battled incessant rain and difficult visibility to win the women’s trap individual gold.The Indian shooter remained composed despite the conditions and finished with 28 hits in the final, setting an Asian Games record in the process.It was a landmark result for Indian shooting as Dhanda became the country’s first-ever women’s trap champion at the Asian Games. Her victory was also India’s first individual shooting gold of the ongoing edition.Dhanda’s success came on a day when the weather repeatedly tested athletes across disciplines, but she managed to maintain her concentration when it mattered most.India added another shooting medal on the day, with Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer taking silver in the women’s trap team event.India’s second gold came in the evening through the women’s 4x400m relay team of Kiran, Prachi Choudhary, MR Poovamma and Vithya Ramraj.The quartet clocked 3:29.69 to finish on top and provide India with its first athletics gold of the Games.For Poovamma, the victory added another chapter to an impressive Asian Games career. The 36-year-old had also been part of India’s gold-medal winning 4x400m relay teams at the 2014 and 2018 editions.Vithya, meanwhile, capped a memorable Games campaign with another medal after earlier bettering PT Usha’s more than four-decade-old national record in the women’s 400m hurdles.The relay gold provided a much-needed high point for India’s athletics campaign, which has otherwise produced a mixed set of results in Aichi-Nagoya.Nineteen-year-old high jumper Pooja Singh added a bronze after clearing 1.84m, while Gulveer Singh continued his remarkable run by winning bronze in the men’s 5000m.Gulveer had already won silver in the 10,000m and 1500m and thus completed a treble of track and field medals at these Games.His achievement put him in elite company. Gulveer became only the second Indian man to win three track and field medals at a single Asian Games after Lavy Pinto, who won gold in the 100m and 200m and silver in the 4x100m relay at the inaugural 1951 edition.India also secured bronze in the mixed 4x100m relay, with Gurindervir Singh, Sneha Sathyanarayana, Animesh Kujur and Harita Bhadra clocking a season-best 41.06 seconds.The men’s 4x400m relay quartet of Vishal TK, Dharamveer Choudhary, Jay Kumar and T Manu also finished with bronze in 3:01.61. India could not defend the gold won at the previous edition.The country, however, drew a blank in both the men’s and women’s 800m finals.The athletics medal haul remained well short of India’s six golds from the previous edition, but the women’s relay triumph ensured the campaign ended Day 10 on a high.India’s boxing campaign also received a major boost as Ankush Panghal reached the men’s 80kg final, ending an eight-year wait for an Indian male boxing finalist at the Asian Games.Ankush produced a stirring comeback to defeat reigning 75kg world champion Fazliddin Erkinboev of Uzbekistan 4-1 and book his place in the gold-medal bout.Parveen Hooda also advanced to the final of the women’s 65kg category after a commanding 5-0 victory over China’s Li Shu.Narender Berwal, meanwhile, signed off with a bronze after losing 0-5 to reigning super-heavyweight world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan in the +90kg semifinal.The medal was Narender’s second Asian Games bronze after he also finished on the podium at Hangzhou in 2023.India’s boxers have now ensured six medals at these Games, surpassing their previous haul of four.The Indian men’s volleyball team also advanced to the quarterfinals after producing a remarkable comeback against Qatar.India recovered from two sets down to defeat Qatar 26-28, 25-27, 25-23, 25-20, 24-22 in a marathon Pool C encounter that lasted two hours and 47 minutes.The victory completed a perfect group-stage run for India, which had earlier defeated Vietnam 3-0 and Hong Kong China 3-0.All four quarterfinals will be played on Thursday.India also made progress in the recurve events, with Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Kumkum Mohod Anil advancing to the quarterfinals.Chauhan produced one of the biggest results of the day when he stunned South Korea’s Kim Je Deok, a three-time Olympic gold-medallist, 6-4 in the men’s individual 1/8 elimination round.Bommadevara also advanced after defeating Chinese Taipei’s Cheng Hsiang-Hui 6-2.In the women’s recurve event, Kumkum Mohod Anil defeated Bangladesh’s Saima Salah Uddin 6-0 to reach the last eight.The Indian women’s squash team completed a 3-0 win over Iran in its final group-stage match to advance to the quarterfinals.Tanvi Khanna was declared the winner after Iran’s Narges Soltani retired while trailing. Anahat Singh then defeated Fereshteh Eghtedari 3-0 before veteran Joshna Chinappa completed the clean sweep with a 3-0 win over Najmeh Boushehrizadeh.India will face Singapore in the quarterfinals on Wednesday.In tennis, Dhakshineswar Suresh and Sumit Nagal made winning starts to their men’s singles campaigns and secured places in the pre-quarterfinals.Dhakshineswar defeated Indonesia’s Gunawan Trismuwantara 7-5, 7-6(2), while Nagal overcame South Korea’s Seongchan Hong 6-4, 6-0 in a rain-interrupted contest.Cycling, however, provided disappointment, with India’s riders failing to advance from the preliminary stages in the men’s and women’s team sprint and women’s team pursuit events.
Article Summary: Neeru Dhanda wins India's first-ever Asian Games gold in women's trap event. India's women's 4x400m relay team adds another gold in the evening to make Tuesday a fruitful Day 10 for India at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. India ended the day with 53 medals — six gold, 21 silver and 26 bronze — to sit 10th in the table.

Article Title: Brazil to bring security team to avoid Messi-like fiasco
Article Text:
Brazil will play a friendly against India on October 3

Panaji:

TOI

The Brazil national football team has been assured of top-notch security by authorities in India, but the five-time world champions are not leaving anything to chance.An eight-member security delegation from Brazil will arrive in Kolkata before the national team to ensure that the star footballers are well protected when they step into the country.A star-studded Brazilian squad captained by Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) defender Marquinhos and including Real Madrid attacker Vinicius Junior, Barcelona forward Raphinha, and Arsenal pair Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimaraes will arrive in Kolkata on Oct 1.The Selecao will play a friendly against India on Oct 3.“Brazil will have a security team comprising experts and former Army officials,” a source who is involved in organisation of the match told. “They will be in Kolkata early on Wednesday, much before the team arrives. Their job is to ensure the safety of the players, delegates, and work with the police to ensure that security is as per international standards.”Last December, Lionel Messi’s visit to the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata during the India tour descended into mayhem as angry fans ripped up seats and invaded the field, prompting the Argentina superstar to cut short his visit. Thousands of fans were angry as their view of the star footballer was blocked by dozens of VIPs and organisers who were seen jostling for a selfie.“Extra precautions are being taken,” said another official.The hotel where Brazil will stay for three days will be turned into a fortress. According to sources, the Brazil football federation (CBF) has asked for a “secure training centre, situated no more than 25 minutes travelling time from the hotel and 24-hour security on all floors of the hotel where the team will stay.”At the stadium, restrooms and other public facilities are being renovated, while new fencing is being installed around the practice grounds as part of the security arrangements.Brazil played two friendlies against Australia as part of their Asia tour and are now headed to India for a historic clash against India. The former world champions are ranked fifth in the world, while India are at 137.Last week, India held World Cuppers Panama, ranked world no. 40, to a 1-1 draw at the Sree Kanteerava stadium in Bengaluru.

Article Title: Al Fursan-led consortium acquires Kerala Blasters FC from Magnum Group
Article Text:
Kerala Blasters FC Vibin Mohanan, third left, celebrates with teammates after scoring the second goal during Indian Super League (ISL) match between Kerala Blasters FC and Jamshedpur FC, In Kochi, Kerala. (PTI File Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOCHI: A consortium led by UAE-based Al Fursan Group has taken complete ownership of Kerala Blasters FC , one of the most popular clubs in the Indian Super League . The announcement was made at a news conference in Kochi on Tuesday. Club officials did not disclose the value of the transaction, but sources indicate that the deal is worth about Rs 120 crore, placing it among the largest foreign investments in Indian football in recent years.The takeover ends the tenure of Hyderabad-based Magnum Sports, which had owned and managed the club since 2016. Kerala Blasters CEO Abhik Chatterjee said the ownership transfer will be carried out in phases and is expected to be completed over the next eight months.Under the new arrangement, the club’s operations will be managed by Ofioh Sporty. Its CEO, Thameem Anvar, said the new owners have plans to develop a dedicated stadium for the Blasters. He added that more details would be revealed once “Project Blasters” is formally announced.There had been speculation that the club could shift its base to Kozhikode, but Chatterjee clarified that Kochi will remain Kerala Blasters’ home.The team will continue to play its home matches at the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium. Addressing expectations for the upcoming season, he said the club’s ambition to win remains strong, though preparations are limited by time. He also confirmed that Ashley Westwood will continue as head coach and will take decisions on squad matters.Chatterjee dismissed reports suggesting that the Blasters’ opening home match could be postponed. He said delaying the fixture would be unfair to other teams because the league schedule has already been released.Al Fursan Group is understood to have backing from business interests connected to Sharjah’s ruling Al Qasimi family. Its entry gives a Gulf-based investment group control of a club with one of the largest fan bases in Indian football.The acquisition comes as Kerala Blasters prepare for the 2026-27 ISL season. Magnum Sports had been seeking a buyer, and interested parties completed financial, legal and operational due diligence before the sale was finalised.
Article Summary: consortium led by UAE-based Al Fursan Group has taken complete ownership of Kerala Blasters FC. Club officials did not disclose the value of the transaction, but sources indicate that the deal is worth about Rs 120 crore. The takeover ends the tenure of Hyderabad-based Magnum Sports, which had owned and managed the club since 2016.

Article Title: FIFA hits back at UEFA: Infantino's lawyers accuse European body of 'harassment'
Article Text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino

What is the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIFA lawyers have accused UEFA of harassing president Gianni Infantino and urged a Florida judge to reject the European soccer body's request for evidence related to a proposed private investment plan involving the 2026 World Cup, news agency Assocuated Press reported.In a 21-page filing submitted late Monday (local time) to the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, FIFA lawyers said UEFA was wrong to suggest that Infantino sought to personally profit from the project, which caused a backlash in July before being dropped within days.UEFA has since asked three courts, including courts in Manhattan and Miami, to authorize discovery as it seeks information to help prepare a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland over alleged financial mismanagement. One of the requests targets Josh Kushner's New York-based investment firm, while another relates to FIFA's office base in Miami.“UEFA’s conduct demonstrates that its (court filing) was made in bad faith and for the purpose of harassment,” FIFA lawyers said in the filing.The filing also pointed to the Nov. 18 deadline for candidates to enter the FIFA presidential election, which will be held in March in Morocco. Infantino is seeking a fourth and final term that would keep him in office through 2031.“This court should reject any attempt to influence FIFA’s presidential election based on these grounds,” FIFA lawyers wrote.UEFA led the backlash against the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which was proposed by Infantino. The plan involved creating a new FIFA subsidiary and selling at least 20% of FIFA's future commercial rights for $4.2 billion to a group of investors led by Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.UEFA said in court filings last month that the proposed valuation was a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.” The claim came amid speculation that Infantino could take a CEO-like role at the new subsidiary with a salary higher than his current $6 million presidential pay package.FIFA lawyers rejected that suggestion, saying UEFA “falsely asserts that Mr. Infantino sought to have a personal financial interest in the FFE project.”The plan was first reported by the media on July 28. It led to criticism from FIFA's then-chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, who was later removed from his position. Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro, a former Goldman Sachs partner, also resigned in protest, saying the deal was bad for soccer.Infantino later apologised for errors in the way the plan was handled and offered to open an independent external review of FIFA's governance.FIFA has maintained that the proposed commercial spinoff was intended to accelerate the development of soccer around the world, particularly outside Europe's wealthier football markets.
Article Summary: FIFA lawyers have accused UEFA of harassing president Gianni Infantino. They have urged a Florida judge to reject the European soccer body's request for evidence related to a proposed private investment plan involving the 2026 World Cup. UEFA led the backlash against the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which was proposed by Infantinos.UEFA has since asked three courts, including courts in Manhattan and Miami, to authorize discovery.
