Article Title: Irish football body launches review over alleged racist ‘monkey chants’ after UEFA refuses to investigate Ireland-Israel clash
Article Text:
Players of Israel, right, and Ireland stand for the anthems before the UEFA Nations League soccer match between Ireland and Israel in Debrecen, Hungary, Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. (Zsolt Czegledi/MTI via AP)

FAI review allegations after Molumby raises concern during match

The Irish Times

X/@Red_united03 | According to FAI, Irish midfielder Jayson Molumby heard chants directed at Adam Idah.

Israeli supporters also filmed military chants after the defeat

Ireland's players had already taken several symbolic actions

Jake O'Brien and Manor Solomon also clashed during the match

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Football Association of Ireland is reviewing footage and audio recordings after an allegation that Irish forward Adam Idah was subjected to racist chanting during Ireland’s 3–0 Nations League win over Israel. The claim emerged after midfielder Jayson Molumby alerted match officials during the game, while UEFA has told the FAI that its own disciplinary process cannot begin because the required reporting procedure was not followed.The allegation centres on events during Ireland’s 3–0 victory over Israel at the Nagyerdei Stadium in Debrecen, Hungary, on Sunday.Idah, who scored Ireland’s second goal, is reported to have been targeted by chants from sections of the Israeli support. The 25-year-old, who was born to a Nigerian father and an Irish mother, was said to be unaware of the alleged abuse while the match was taking place.According to, Molumby heard what he believed were racist chants aimed at Idah before half-time. The Ireland midfielder approached referee Harm Osmers and fourth official Florian Exner and asked them to “listen”, pointing towards the stands.The officials did not hear chanting that they considered racist and the incident was not formally reported on the pitch as a racial-abuse allegation.A UEFA match delegate later informed the FAI that the matter could not be investigated through UEFA's disciplinary process because the correct protocol had not been followed. Molumby had not explicitly identified the chanting as racist when speaking to the officials, while the officials themselves had not heard the alleged abuse.The FAI has since decided to conduct its own review. The association is examining available video and audio footage to establish what was said in the stands and whether Idah was subjected to racist abuse.Al Jazeera has reported that videos circulating on social media appear to show Israeli supporters directing “monkey chants” towards Idah during the match.The allegations surrounding Idah emerged alongside another incident involving supporters in the Israeli section of the stadium.Youseph Haddad, who is described in the reporting as a member of an Israeli right-wing party and a candidate for the country's upcoming parliamentary elections, filmed himself among supporters during the match and posted footage on social media.The video showed supporters chanting about the Israeli military as their team fell to a 3–0 defeat.“Yes, we lose in football, but where we don’t lose, the IDF [Israeli Defence Force]. We always win,” Haddad said in the video.“So maybe the football Irish team beat us on the football field, but they will never, ever break the Israeli spirit.”It is not clear whether the chants about the Israeli military would fall within UEFA's rules on spectator behaviour. UEFA's disciplinary regulations allow sanctions ranging from fines to stadium closures and restrictions on away supporters when national associations are found responsible for prohibited spectator conduct, but such penalties require a disciplinary process.The match itself had already attracted significant attention before kick-off because of political pressure surrounding Ireland's decision to fulfil its Nations League fixtures against Israel.The FAI had previously asked UEFA whether Ireland and Israel could be kept apart in future competition draws. UEFA rejected that request, saying such decisions were not based on public sentiment and noting that the countries had never been in direct conflict.The events in Debrecen came after days of internal discussions within the Ireland squad over whether the fixture should be played.Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad after speaking with his teammates and explaining that he did not feel he could participate in the matches against Israel.“I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle. Therefore, I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel,” Bazunu said.Ireland ultimately went ahead with the match after discussions between the players and the FAI. The decision came after months of pressure from campaigners calling for the fixtures to be boycotted in response to Israel's war in Gaza.On the pitch, Ireland's players wore black armbands, with FAI chief executive David Courell saying they were worn in recognition of “all lives lost” in the conflict. The players also bowed their heads during Israel's national anthem and did not shake hands with their opponents before kick-off.Ireland captain Dara O'Shea did not shake hands with Israel captain Dor Peretz, while reports also said O'Shea had pledged to donate his match earnings to humanitarian aid for Gaza.The match itself remained one-sided. Troy Parrott opened the scoring, Idah added the second and Jack Moylan completed the 3–0 victory.The political tension surrounding the fixture spilled into an on-field exchange involving Ireland defender Jake O'Brien and Israel winger Manor Solomon.Reports said the two players became involved in an angry confrontation during the match, with O'Brien allegedly telling Solomon: “Shame on you for what you’re doing in Gaza. You deserve to lose.”Solomon responded: “Come out, be a man. Don’t talk behind a wall. It’s a shame the game wasn’t in Israel, you would understand what the best country in the world is.”Speaking after the match, Solomon declined to repeat what had been said during the confrontation but made clear that the relationship between the two sides had become hostile.“They said nonsense during the game, I don’t want to comment on them,” Solomon said.He further added that he held back from saying more because of the possibility of suspension.“If I say what I think about them I’ll probably be banned for a few games so I don’t want to say, of course they hate us and we don’t like them.”Solomon also looked ahead to the return fixture.“I’m already looking forward to the next game against them, it’s going to be completely different.”He later added: “They (the Irish players) don’t interest me. We have a country ten times better than theirs, stronger, an amazing country with amazing people.”“We are proud to wear the team shirt and to be Israelis. We are proud of our state and of our soldiers.”“They can play all their tricks. We are Israelis and love the country. And that will always be the case.”Ireland's next Nations League match is against Austria at the Aviva Stadium on October 1, while Israel will host Kosovo on the same day.The return fixture between Ireland and Israel is scheduled for October 4 at the TSC Arena in Bačka Topola, Serbia. The FAI had moved the nominal home fixture there because of what it described as operational challenges, while Israel have continued to play their home internationals at neutral venues because of security concerns.
Article Summary: FAI reviewing footage and audio recordings after allegation that Irish forward Adam Idah was subjected to racist chanting during Ireland’s 3–0 Nations League win over Israel. The claim emerged after midfielder Jayson Molumby alerted match officials during the game. UEFA has told the FAI that its own disciplinary process cannot begin because the required reporting procedure was not followed.

Article Title: First time in football history: Two players sent off for pulling the same opponent with ridiculous 5ft-long dreadlocks
Article Text:
Anguilla’s Aedan Scipio made football history during their Concacaf Nations League clash with Antigua, as Keon Greene and Shalon Knight were sent off for pulling his 5ft dreadlocks

Aedan Scipio’s hair became the target twice

Scipio became an unlikely viral sensation

Why hair-pulling can lead to a straight red card

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Antigua and Barbuda still finished with a 5–0 victory

Aedan Scipio had only been on the pitch for a few minutes when his extraordinary dreadlocks became the centre of a bizarre international match. The 36-year-old Anguilla forward came off the bench against Antigua and Barbuda with his side already 5–0 down, but two opponents were later sent off for pulling his hair. Both incidents involved Scipio’s ankle-length dreadlocks, turning an otherwise one-sided Concacaf Nations League match into an unusual piece of football history.Scipio entered the match in the 69th minute at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, with Anguilla already facing a heavy deficit against Antigua and Barbuda.The 36-year-old, who plays for the Roaring Lions, is known for dreadlocks that stretch almost 1.5 metres and come close to his ankles when left loose. When tied back, the hair is often wrapped around his waist with a band, although even then it remains close enough to the ground to be grabbed by an opponent.That became particularly relevant in the second half.According to ESPN, Scipio had regained possession in his own area after being dispossessed when Antigua and Barbuda midfielder Keon Greene grabbed his hair and pulled him backwards. Scipio reacted angrily to the challenge, and the referee immediately showed Greene a straight red card in the 71st minute.The incident might have been strange enough on its own, but it was repeated later in the match.Deep into stoppage time, Scipio was advancing up the pitch when Antigua and Barbuda's Shalon Knight grabbed another section of his dreadlocks. The pull sent Scipio crashing to the ground, and Knight was shown a straight red card.Antigua and Barbuda finished with nine players, but the match had already produced a bizarre piece of football history: for the first time, two players had been sent off in the same game for pulling the hair of the same opponent. Both incidents involved Scipio and his extraordinary dreadlocks.The unusual sequence quickly spread online, with footage of both incidents attracting attention well beyond the Concacaf Nations League.Social-media users began referring to Anguilla as having found a "cheat code", because Scipio had entered the game with his team already five goals behind and subsequently contributed to two opposing players being dismissed.The joke, however, came from a very real physical problem created by the length of Scipio's hair.His dreadlocks are long enough to remain within an opponent's reach during a challenge, particularly when they are tied behind him. That does not make grabbing them permissible, but it helps explain why something rarely seen in professional football happened twice during the same matchScipio's appearance has also made him one of the more recognisable players in Anguilla's squad. The island nation remains among the lowest-ranked teams in international football, with ESPN reporting that Anguilla entered the match ranked 210th in the world, with only San Marino below them in FIFA's rankings.Antigua and Barbuda were ranked 163rd and entered the match as the higher-ranked side.The referee's decisions were not based on Scipio having unusually long hair, but on the nature of the challenges themselves.Under football's Laws of the Game, pulling an opponent's hair can constitute violent conduct when the action involves excessive force or brutality and is not an attempt to play the ball. A sufficiently serious hair pull can therefore result in a straight red card.The issue has become more prominent in English football in recent seasons.Three Premier League players were sent off for hair-pulling incidents during the previous season, involving Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare, Everton defender Michael Keane, Sunderland's Dan Ballard and Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez in separate incidents.Keane's dismissal was subsequently appealed, with the argument made that there had not been sufficient intent or force to justify a red card. The appeal against the dismissal was unsuccessful, as was a separate attempt to have his three-match suspension reduced.The Football Association panel considering the case included three former players and voted 2–1 that the red card had not been incorrect and that a three-match suspension was not excessive.Not every contact with an opponent's hair automatically produces the same punishment. The Premier League has introduced clearer guidance under which a hair pull that is not considered excessive can result in a yellow card, while more serious conduct can be treated as violent conduct and punished with a dismissal.In Scipio's case, both Antigua and Barbuda players were sent off after physically pulling him backwards, with Knight's challenge in particular taking the Anguilla player off his feet.The two red cards did not change the outcome of the match.Antigua and Barbuda had already built a five-goal advantage before Scipio entered the game, and even after being reduced to nine players they held on to win 5–0 at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium.The victory came in League C, Group B of the Concacaf Nations League, giving Jacques Passy's side a comfortable result despite the extraordinary finish.For Anguilla, the scoreline remained the dominant fact of the night, but Scipio's brief cameo ensured that the match would be remembered for something else as well.Antigua and Barbuda will now face the consequences of losing Greene and Knight to suspension, with both players set to miss the next meeting with Anguilla on Friday.
Article Summary: Anguilla's Aedan Scipio had only been on the pitch for a few minutes when his extraordinary dreadlocks became the centre of a bizarre international match. The 36-year-old Anguilla forward came off the bench against Antigua and Barbuda with his side already 5–0 down. Keon Greene and Shalon Knight were later sent off for pulling his hair.

Article Title: Cape Verde World Cup hero Vozinha has 28m followers, new club and Ballon d’Or nomination but now wants his old life back
Article Text:
Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha leaves the field at half time during the World Cup round of 32 soccer match against Argentina in Miami Gardens, Fla., Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Seven saves against Spain changed Vozinha's life

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha takes a selfie with fans after the World Cup Group H soccer match between Cape Verde and Saudi Arabia in Houston, Friday, June 26, 2026. (AP Photo/David J. Phillip)

The Observer

The Observer

The fame followed him away from the football pitch

The Observer

His World Cup turned into a new career

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha poses for photos during his presentation as a new player for Colo Colo at Monumental stadium in Santiago, Chile, Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Esteban Felix)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Six months ago, Vozinha was a goalkeeper playing in Portugal's second tier, living quietly in the small city of Chaves with little attention beyond Cape Verde. Then came seven saves against Spain at the World Cup, a million Instagram followers in a day and a level of fame he never expected. Now, with more than 28 million followers, he says he would choose his old life back.For anyone who follows football, Vozinha is now one of the recognisable faces of Cape Verde's remarkable World Cup story. Before the tournament, however, the 40-year-old goalkeeper was largely unknown outside his country and the Portuguese football circuit, where his professional life was centred on the small city of Chaves and the second tier.His real name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, but it was the name Vozinha that suddenly became familiar around the world after Cape Verde's opening group match against Spain.The goalkeeper produced seven saves and kept a clean sheet against the side that would eventually become world champions, turning what had been an ordinary international fixture into the performance that transformed his life. Before kick-off, his Instagram account had around 56,000 followers.Within 24 hours, that number had passed one million.The explosion began with CazéTV, the Brazilian broadcaster that held rights to the tournament, encouraging its audience to follow Vozinha during the historic goalless draw.He did not initially understand what was happening.“A member of the team’s catering staff came up to me and told me I had a billion followers,” Vozinha told. “I had no idea what he was talking about; I thought he was joking, but he insisted. Later, I went to do some interviews in the mixed zone and a CazéTV journalist asked me if I knew what was happening.”The journalist showed him her phone, and that was when Vozinha saw that more than one million people were suddenly following his account.“She showed me her phone and that was when I saw that I had more than a million followers. I decided to turn off my Instagram notifications so I wouldn’t be tempted to keep checking who was following me.”The number did not stop there. Vozinha now has more than 28 million Instagram followers, putting him ahead of prominent American sports figures including Travis Kelce Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady.The attention became so overwhelming that Vozinha, together with the Cape Verdean Football Federation, brought back his former manager to help deal with the sudden noise surrounding him and the team. Someone close to the dressing room told: “It wasn’t easy to get back to normal.”Even with his notifications switched off, friends continued telling him which famous people had started following him, while companies and brands began approaching him with commercial opportunities.“I know that during the World Cup there were lots of companies and brands that wanted to work with me,” Vozinha said, “but while we were competing I only did one promotional collaboration, with UFL Mobile. I don’t know what offers might come in the future, but for now I don’t want to work with any tobacco, alcohol or betting brands.”The World Cup gave Vozinha a new professional profile, but it also changed the most ordinary parts of his life.Speaking to, he explained that going out for dinner or simply being in public now comes with a level of attention he never experienced before.“I’ve lost my peace and tranquillity,” he said. “I no longer have any privacy, or at least much less than I used to. Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there’s always someone who wants to take a photo with me or asks me for an autograph. Or, worse, someone is filming me.“That’s what has changed most in my life, and I don’t think there’s anything I can do about it.”The attention has also reached his family in Cape Verde.His mother, who Vozinha describes as someone who finds it difficult to say no to people, now has supporters arriving at her home almost every day asking for photographs or wanting to speak with her. His father, who is more reserved, has learned to keep his distance.“I’m not there, so I can’t help them,” Vozinha said. “They have to learn to live with the situation and set boundaries.”That loss of privacy has made the goalkeeper unusually candid about the less attractive side of becoming famous, particularly because fame was never something he appears to have been seeking.“A lot of people want to be famous and have a public profile, but they only see the positive side of that reality,” Vozinha said. “To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I’d choose the one I had before.”For all the attention surrounding him, Vozinha has also been careful not to turn Cape Verde's World Cup into an individual achievement.The country went unbeaten in Group H, reached the knockout stage and produced one of the tournament's most unexpected stories. Vozinha was the standout performer, keeping two clean sheets and making 18 saves across the tournament before Cape Verde eventually lost 3-2 to Argentina after a late own goal from Diney Borges.“It’s nice to feel like a kind of ambassador, but I want to make it clear that what we achieved was a collective effort,” Vozinha said.“We made history and the best news would be if we could harness that momentum to develop our country and improve the living conditions of our people.”The attention around Vozinha did not disappear when Cape Verde's tournament ended.His performances helped earn him a move to Colo-Colo, the biggest and most successful football club in Chile, after the club showed the strongest interest in signing him.“They were the club that showed the most interest,” Vozinha said. “I didn’t receive any offers from the United States and there was some contact with Saudi Arabia, but nothing concrete. Hopefully I can play in the Copa Libertadores soon.”His international career also continued, despite the fact that he had initially planned to retire after the World Cup.Instead, the 40-year-old decided he still wanted to play and was preparing in Lisbon for the start of Cape Verde's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.“I still feel good,” he said.There was another unexpected development waiting for him, too. With a month remaining before the Ballon d'Or ceremony, Vozinha was named among the 10 nominees for the world's best goalkeeper.“I never imagined it could happen,” he said. “It was unthinkable, but I’m grateful to those who thought of me. Just being on that list is already a great honour.”His new career has therefore brought opportunities that would have been difficult to imagine before the World Cup, from a move to Colo-Colo and the possibility of playing in the Copa Libertadores to becoming one of the most recognisable players from Cape Verde's historic campaign.But the attention has come with a price that cannot be measured in followers, contracts or endorsements.
Article Summary: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha has more than 28 million Instagram followers. The 40-year-old was largely unknown outside his country and the Portuguese football circuit. The World Cup gave him a new professional profile, but it also changed the most ordinary parts of his life.

Article Title: ‘Because of agents and family issues’: Brazil football legend Roberto Carlos reveals shocking loss of 99% of his $180m career earnings
Article Text:
Brazil legend Roberto Carlos reveals how he lost 99% of his football earnings/ Image: X, Instagram

Carlos says people he trusted emptied his bank account

His playing career generated enormous wealth

The career behind the fortune was extraordinary

Former Brazil player Roberto Carlos arrives to attend the draw for the 2026 soccer World Cup at the Kennedy Center in Washington, Friday, Dec. 5, 2025. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Roberto Carlos made a fortune during a 24-year career spent winning almost everything there was to win, but the former Brazil and Real Madrid star says almost all of it is now gone. The 53-year-old has revealed that he lost 99% of what he earned from football, while giving only a limited explanation of how his finances unravelled and pointing instead to serious family problems, agents and people he trusted.Speaking at the Portugal Football Summit in Lisbon, Carlos opened up about his finances while discussing the importance of planning for life after football and protecting a player's image beyond the pitch."I had problems with people who emptied my bank account. I lost 99% of everything I earned from football," Carlos said.He did not provide a full breakdown of what happened to his money, but said agents and family issues were central to the financial problems he experienced."Because of agents and family issues, I lost 99% of everything I had earned in football," he added.Carlos also described the moment he realised the scale of what had happened, saying that it came with almost no warning."I had a very serious family problem. One Thursday, I went to bed at midnight and the next day, I received a pile of documents I knew nothing about. That's when I realised I had lost my entire history."Carlos did not identify the family members involved or explain precisely what the documents contained, so his comments do not establish that his children, wives or other relatives were personally responsible for the losses.His personal life has been unusually large by any measure, with Carlos having 11 children, relationships with seven women and two marriages, but he has not publicly attributed the financial problems to any particular member of his family.Reports from Globo have also pointed to problems involving agents and advisers, although Carlos himself has remained relatively vague about the precise circumstances.The numbers involved make the admission particularly striking. Estimates put Carlos' career football earnings at around $180 million, meaning that losing 99% would amount to more than $178 million and leave roughly $1.8 million from that original sum.Celebrity Net Worth, meanwhile, currently estimates his net worth at $5 million, although that figure is separate from Carlos' own account of losing 99% of his football earnings.Carlos had the kind of career that made significant wealth possible, particularly during the peak years of European football's spending boom.He spent 11 seasons with Real Madrid, making 527 appearances and winning four La Liga titles and three Champions League trophies. He played alongside Zinedine Zidane , Luis Figo, Ronaldo and David Beckham during the club's famous Galácticos era and became one of the defining left-backs of his generation.When Carlos renewed his Real Madrid contract in 2000, he reportedly received an $8.5 million signing bonus alongside a $5.1 million annual salary, with the club also covering his home rent and six trips to São Paulo each season.After leaving Madrid in 2007, he joined Fenerbahçe, where he earned €4.2 million net per season.Even later in his career, the money remained substantial. In 2011, at the age of 37, Russian club Anzhi Makhachkala offered him a contract worth €6 million per year, then approximately $9 million.Carlos eventually continued playing into his 40s, making his final appearances as a player-manager in India in 2015.Across those years, his football career is estimated to have generated around $180 million, a figure that reflects both his club contracts and the extraordinary commercial value attached to one of the sport's most recognisable defenders.Carlos' financial story is difficult to separate from just how successful he was as a footballer.For Brazil, he played at three World Cups and helped the country win the 2002 tournament after reaching the final four years earlier. He made more than 120 appearances for the national team and spent much of his peak being regarded as not only the world's leading left-back but one of the best players in football.He came close to major individual honours as well. Carlos finished second to Ronaldo in the 1997 FIFA World Player of the Year voting and again finished second to his Brazilian teammate for the 2002 Ballon d'Or after winning the World Cup.His most famous moment may have come in 1997, when his free-kick against France appeared to be travelling several yards wide before swerving dramatically back towards the goal. The strike became one of football's most famous goals and was subsequently studied by physicists because of the unusual trajectory.Away from the pitch, Carlos says he had always understood that his playing career would eventually end and that he needed something to fall back on."I made mistakes, and therefore, I ask younger players not to do the same. I always thought about future plans after my playing career," he said.Carlos said he had already obtained his sporting director's licence by the time he decided to leave football and was working with several brands, allowing him to build a second career around his name and reputation."It's about building a history as a player and leveraging your image," he said. "When I decided to leave football, I already had my sporting director's licence and was working with many brands."Carlos now works in football and continues to operate as a brand ambassador, including in his role with Real Madrid as an ambassador for Asia and Oceania and director of institutional relations.His warning to younger players is consequently less about the size of a footballer's salary than what happens around it. Carlos earned millions at some of the biggest clubs in the world, built a career that produced World Cup and Champions League titles, and became one of the most recognisable players of his era.Yet he says that people he trusted, agents and serious family problems ultimately left him with only a fraction of what that career had generated.Carlos has not provided all the details behind the losses, but his message at the Portugal Football Summit was clear enough: earning a fortune during a football career is one thing, protecting it when other people have access to your finances is another.
Article Summary: Brazil legend Roberto Carlos reveals how he lost 99% of his football earnings. Carlos says people he trusted emptied his bank account. The 53-year-old made a fortune during a 24-year career spent winning almost everything there was to win. Estimates put Carlos' career football earnings at around $180 million.

Article Title: Could Erling Haaland be forced to leave Manchester City for Real Madrid, Barcelona or PSG if the club is relegated?
Article Text:
Manchester City's Erling Haaland warms up prior to the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Bournemouth in Manchester, England, Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

Haaland chose City despite knowing the 115-charge case was hanging over the club

Manchester City have officially confirmed the signing of Erling Haaland |courtesy-@ManCity on Twitter

A heavy punishment could change the equation completely

Manchester City's Erling Haaland walks off the pitch after the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Sunderland in Manchester, England, Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

Real Madrid, Barcelona and PSG would be the obvious destinations

PSG have the money, while Bayern, Chelsea, Arsenal and even Leeds remain longer shots

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Erling Haaland signed one of the longest contracts in Premier League history because he believed in Manchester City's plans for the future, but the circumstances around the club have changed dramatically since then. Reports that City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial charges have brought the possibility of serious sporting sanctions back into focus, with the club expected to appeal and no punishment yet decided.But if the eventual punishment were severe enough to push City out of the Premier League, the conversation around their biggest players would change quickly. Haaland, more than almost anyone else in the squad, would become the centre of it.In January 2025, the Norwegian signed a new nine-and-a-half-year contract that runs until the summer of 2034, committing him to City for what was then described as the longest deal in Premier League history. The club confirmed the agreement and Haaland said he was happy to continue his career at the Etihad.When he was asked whether the 115 charges had influenced his decision to sign such an extraordinary contract, Haaland made clear that they had not."No, I haven't thought of that or anything," he said. "I am confident that the club know what they are doing and I really don't think I should speak too much about this."He maintained that position in March 2025 when reporters asked whether he was concerned about the possibility of a significant punishment."I don't do that, obviously, when I sign a nine-and-a-half-year contract," Haaland said. "I've said 300 times why I signed the contract. I talked to the club, got a good feeling and agreed to it in the end. That's why."By July, when he spoke to TIME , Haaland was still relying on those conversations with City's hierarchy."I spoke with the bosses, and in the end, I believe them," he said. "It's such a tricky situation for me to even sit there and speak about, because I wasn't really involved."Haaland also did not sign his new deal expecting to leave anytime soon. His contract runs until 2034, and City presented it as a long-term commitment when the extension was announced. Reports at the time also suggested that the release clauses included in his previous agreement had been removed.There have, however, been reports of a separate mechanism that could allow Haaland to leave around 2030 for a fee that would gradually decrease. So, what happens if City are actually relegated? There is reportedly no clause in Haaland’s contract that would allow him to walk away automatically if that happens. City sources have also maintained that Haaland and the club’s other key players do not have release clauses.There have, however, been reports of a separate mechanism that could allow Haaland to leave around 2030 for a fee that would gradually decrease.There’s still a long way to go before City know what punishment, if any, they will face. The reported findings are not the final word, and the club is expected to appeal. For now, that leaves the biggest question hanging over the whole situation: just how serious will the eventual punishment be?If the eventual outcome were a fine or a relatively manageable points deduction, there would be little reason to assume Haaland's position had fundamentally changed.A far more serious sporting punishment would be different.A sufficiently large points deduction could threaten City's Premier League survival, while expulsion from the division would create an even more dramatic situation. Previous reporting on the case has identified sanctions ranging from financial penalties and points deductions to more severe sporting consequences, including demotion.Money would be another big part of the equation. If City were relegated, the financial hit would be huge. The club could be forced to cut its wage bill, and Haaland’s reported £525,000-a-week ($710,000) salary would make him an obvious part of that conversation. Selling him would also bring in a massive transfer fee, making the Norwegian one of the biggest financial decisions City could face.The absence of a relegation clause means the club would still have considerable control over any transfer, and City have shown little indication that they intend to dismantle their squad simply because the legal process has reached a new stage. But if the financial and sporting consequences became severe enough, selling one of the world's most valuable players could become a very different proposition.And if Haaland himself decided that remaining outside the Premier League was not compatible with his ambitions, the situation could develop into the kind of blockbuster transfer that few clubs could afford to ignore.There would be no shortage of interest if Haaland ever became available, but the combination of his wages and the transfer fee would immediately reduce the list of realistic destinations.Paris Saint-Germain would have the financial capacity to enter the conversation, while their status at the top of European football would give Haaland a route to remain in the Champions League rather than taking a step down with City.Then there are the two Spanish giants that have been linked with him for years.Barcelona president Joan Laporta is a known admirer of Haaland, and the club has previously been reported to have considered an attempt to sign the Norwegian. Barcelona's finances, however, would make a deal of this scale particularly difficult. The club has faced significant financial constraints, and finding room for Haaland's wages alongside a potentially enormous transfer fee would require considerable financial manoeuvring.There is also a footballing argument for Barcelona.Haaland would provide the specialist centre-forward presence that Barcelona have looked for at various points, while Raphinha's ability to operate from the wing or centrally could give the team some flexibility around him. Barcelona had also previously shown interest in Julian Alvarez when looking to strengthen the striker position, underlining the importance they have placed on the role.Real Madrid offer a different problem because the question would not simply be whether they can afford Haaland.Madrid have long been linked with the Norwegian, and their financial strength would make a move conceivable, but Kylian Mbappe already occupies a prominent central attacking role alongside Vinicius Junior, Jude Bellingham and the rest of the club's attacking options.Bringing Haaland into that group would therefore require a tactical reshuffle.Both Haaland and Mbappe have built their reputations as the focal points of elite attacks, so fitting them into the same team would be one of the major footballing questions surrounding any potential Madrid move. That does not make a transfer impossible, but it would make the footballing structure as important as the finances.For now, neither Barcelona nor Real Madrid has taken an official step to sign Haaland, and there is no confirmed transfer agreement involving either club.The financial reality means that the list cannot simply include every major European club.Bayern Munich, Chelsea and perhaps Arsenal could emerge as alternatives if Haaland were genuinely placed on the transfer market, although each would face its own financial and sporting considerations. Several Saudi Pro League clubs could also afford the wages and transfer fee, although such a move would represent a different career choice for a player still operating at the centre of European football.Then there is Leeds United, which offers the most personal storyline of all.Haaland was born in Leeds, and he grew up supporting the club where his father, Alfie Haaland, played between 1997 and 2000. A return to Yorkshire would therefore have an obvious emotional appeal and would make for one of the most striking transfers in English football.The financial reality, however, is much harder to overcome.Leeds would have to find a way to match Haaland's enormous wages as well as the transfer fee that City would demand for a player contracted until 2034. Even if the striker had a personal connection to the club, those numbers would make the move extraordinarily difficult.For now, the biggest variable is not Real Madrid, Barcelona or PSG. It is Manchester City's case itself.The reported findings have moved the long-running saga into another stage, but sanctions have not yet been settled and City are expected to appeal. Until that process produces a sporting consequence, Haaland remains a Manchester City player with a contract stretching to 2034.If the punishment ultimately leaves City in the Premier League, the transfer speculation may amount to little more than another round of headlines. If it instead threatens the club's place in English football, Haaland's future becomes one of the most significant questions in the aftermath.And even then, his contract means he would not simply walk away. Any move to Madrid, Barcelona, PSG or elsewhere would still have to be negotiated.
Article Summary: Erling Haaland signed a new nine-and-a-half-year contract that runs until the summer of 2034. He chose City despite knowing the 115-charge case was hanging over the club. Reports that City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial charges have brought the possibility of serious sporting sanctions.

Tom Brady reflects on playing in the last season of his career while dealing with a divorce from Gisele Bundchen

Tom Brady reflects on giving up football entirely as he navigated through a tough marriage

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, has had a lot to deal with in his personal life in the last few years. While he remained unbeatable on the field, Tom Brady’s marriage to ex wife Gisele Bundchen suffered in the public eye. Amid the new speculations about how his high profile marriage ended, Tom Brady’s words on how he survived it has moved many.A few weeks ago, in an interview with MLFootball, the New England Patriots’ legend Tom Brady reflected on how he kept playing in the last year of his career as he got divorced in the middle of the season.Tom Brady said. "My last season was tough. I was going through a lot of just a personal family issue, and it was a challenge, and it was a very… It just took a lot out of me in terms of my ability to continue to play…”In 2022, as the seven time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady returned to the field for one last time, his marriage ended with the Brazilian supermodel in the middle of the season.Many blamed it on how passionate Tom Brady was about his career as he dealt with speculations about allegedly not being able to give time to his wife, Gisele Bundchen, and their children.Despite the constant speculations, the NFL legend Tom Brady kept himself away from it as he has focused on his life now.While Tom Brady’s divorce from his ex wife, Gisele Bundchen, was incredibly hard, the star player also had to navigate through retirement.In the interview, the NFL legend Tom Brady said, "It's hard to give up football, too…”The New England Patriots’ icon added, "It's something that we're really good at. It's something you love to do. You love being out there with your teammates." The former quarterback said he always felt a deep responsibility to those around him.”The seven time Super Bowl champion added, "I felt like I owed it to my teammates and coaches to give them everything I had…”Four years after his divorce, Tom Brady seems to have recovered well from the heartbreak of his marriage ending.In the last few years, he has focused on his career as a sports analyst on FOX Sports while making strategic investments in emerging brands.The NFL legend has also focused on fatherhood and being there for his three children as he spends time with them which he had missed out while playing in the league.
